questions.q: Why does this lesson say formulas are worth learning as "one language, everywhere"?
options: Formulas only work inside formula fields, nowhere else
Validation rules, approval criteria, and formula fields all share the same underlying formula syntax
Every formula must be rewritten in Apex before it can run
Formulas are unique to each tool and don't transfer between them
questions.explain: The same expression syntax (AND, ISBLANK, comparison operators, and so on) is used across validation rules, approval entry criteria, and formula fields.

questions.q: In the Insert Field picker, what does a ">" after an object name like "Account >" indicate?
options: That field is required
That field is a formula field itself
The object has more related fields available if you drill in
The formula has a syntax error
questions.explain: The ">" marker means there are more fields nested under that relationship, letting a formula reach across to a related object.

questions.q: A formula field is defined as Number, but its formula returns a Text value. What kind of error is this?
options: Too many parameters
A missing parenthesis
A misspelled field name
An incorrect result data type
questions.explain: The formula's return type has to match the field's defined data type; a Text result in a Number field is an incorrect result data type error.

questions.q: What makes a formula field different from a regular stored field?
options: It is calculated fresh every time it's displayed, rather than being saved to the database
It cannot appear on a report
It can only be seen by administrators
It only works on the Account object
questions.explain: A formula field is never actually saved; it's recalculated on read wherever it's displayed, so it never goes stale.

questions.q: In the Advanced Formula editor, what does clicking Check Syntax do?
options: Converts the formula from Advanced to Simple mode
Deletes the current formula and starts over
Saves the formula field permanently
Validates the formula for errors without requiring a save
questions.explain: Check Syntax catches errors like mismatched parentheses or incorrect types before you commit the field.
